title: Backwards
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, foggy small American town, cold blue and amber tones, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 4. She played the Mercer tape backwards. Someone was counting. 📼

Original fiction. Part 5 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Mrs. Pruitt told Jenna about the 1911 pact. Then the porch lights of Harlow Creek went dark, one by one, toward them.
scenes.image: an old woman and a young woman at a dark parlor window, porch lights dying one by one down a foggy street

scenes.narration: At noon the lights came back on, like nothing had happened. Mrs. Pruitt wouldn't say another word. So Jenna went back to the only witness she had. The tape.
scenes.image: young woman walking alone down a foggy small-town street at midday, holding an old VHS tape against her chest

scenes.narration: Tom's whisper wouldn't leave her alone. It already lives here. So she did what every podcaster does with a sound that makes no sense. She played it backwards.
scenes.image: a woman's hands threading an old reel of magnetic tape through a vintage tape deck, lamplight, dark room

scenes.narration: Under the hiss there was a second voice. A woman. Soft. Patient. Counting.
scenes.image: close-up of an old speaker grille trembling in a dark room, dust floating in a single beam of lamplight

scenes.narration: Three hundred twelve. Three hundred eleven. Three hundred ten. It was Ruth Mercer. Nobody counts like that unless they're waiting for something.
scenes.image: faded 1980s photograph of a gentle-faced woman with curled hair standing in a farmhouse kitchen

scenes.narration: Jenna listened all night. Ruth never skipped a number. And between each one, so quiet Jenna had to turn it all the way up, a door creaked open.
scenes.image: an old wooden door creaking open into darkness, a thin line of amber light spilling across the floorboards

scenes.narration: At dawn, Jenna walked the whole town with a notebook and counted every open door. Every house. Every shed. The church. Even Mrs. Pruitt's door was standing open now.
scenes.image: young woman with a notebook on a foggy dawn street lined with houses whose front doors stand wide open

scenes.narration: Three hundred eleven. Ruth wasn't counting time. She was counting doors. Every door the Guest walks through.
scenes.image: high view of a foggy small town at dawn, warm light spilling from hundreds of open doorways

scenes.narration: Three hundred twelve doors. Three hundred eleven open. On the tape, Ruth's voice dropped to a whisper. One.
scenes.image: a woman sitting frozen beside an old tape deck in a dark room, her face pale in the amber glow

scenes.narration: Jenna looked down Alder Lane at the only door in Harlow Creek still shut. Her own.
scenes.image: a single closed door at the end of a misty lane at dawn, every other door on the street wide open
